team.summary: Four founders (Bernardo Simonassi, João Borges, Gabriel Lyra, Gustavo Marinho) with a team of 9, accepted into YC W25. Limited public detail on individual backgrounds or prior exits.
team.technicalDepth: [inferred] Building a stablecoin API requires deep blockchain/payments integration expertise; YC acceptance suggests technical credibility.

market.sizeHint: Cross-border payments market worth trillions; stablecoin settlement volume growing rapidly (e.g., $10T+ annualized stablecoin transfer volume).
market.competitiveLandscape: Competes with Circle (USDC), Stripe (crypto), and other crypto payment gateways (e.g., Coinbase Commerce, BitPay). Wedge: developer-first stablecoin API with simple integration.
market.whyNow: Stablecoin adoption accelerating (regulatory clarity in major jurisdictions, growing institutional use), demand for instant/low-cost global payments, and developer preference for API-first financial primitives.

risks.text: Regulatory uncertainty around stablecoins and cross-border payments could limit operations or increase compliance costs.
Intense competition from well-funded incumbents (Circle, Stripe) and other crypto payment startups.
Dependence on underlying blockchain infrastructure (e.g., Ethereum, Solana) for settlement; network congestion or failures could degrade service.
Adoption risk: merchants and developers may prefer established fiat rails or multi-currency solutions over stablecoin-only APIs.

subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: YC W25 acceptance and a team of 9 signal strong early validation; however, limited public information on founder-market fit, prior exits, or deep technical ownership of the core integration layer.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: API integration creates switching costs and potential network effects in a specific vertical (stablecoin payments); no single horizontal platform dependency. Proprietary data moat not yet evident at this early stage.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: Product is a stablecoin API, not an AI-native agent; self-serve onboarding targets developers rather than SMBs; one-liner is clear. Does not meet the thesis's AI-native agent criterion.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: Large, specific vertical (global stablecoin payments) with credible trillion-dollar market size; strong why-now drivers (stablecoin adoption, regulatory progress, demand for faster/cheaper cross-border payments); identifiable competitors and a clear developer-first wedge.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: YC W25 batch (very recent) and team of 9 indicate fresh momentum; no public data on paying customers, revenue, or active usage yet.

scoreRationale: BlindPay scores well on Market & Why-Now (4/5) due to a massive addressable market and timely stablecoin tailwinds. Team (3/5) and Defensibility (3/5) are solid but early with limited public proof. Product (2/5) does not align with the thesis's AI-native agent requirement. Traction (3/5) is fresh but pre-revenue. Overall, a promising fintech infrastructure play that partially fits the thesis.
